Restoring crumb 0x600c (masked since R45A by LATEREL) immediately read 0x0f: apcie_gp_sys, apcie_gpshr_sys, apcie_gp and atc1_usb_aon were ON at commit 1. Root cause: psci_force_ps() (bit 1) and psci_replay_mem() (bit 2), dumped from the HV macOS 14.8.9 guest (booted with apcie=0xfffffffe and USB proxy on ATC0, which never slept in R53c), ran after our quiesce and turned APCIE_GP*, APCIE_GE_SYS, APCIE_ST_SYS, ANS2, ATC0_COMMON/USB, ATC1_USB_AON, SIO and SIO_CPU back on in every run from R45A through R55A. Next: R55B re-runs image 101 with bits 1 and 2 off (fifth word 121).

findings.title: R55B: 0x600c=00 confirmed without psci_force_ps/replay_mem, still no wake; audit found five combined entry bugs fixed in image 102
findings.body: 2026-11-18 (image 101, fifth aura-ctl word 121): PCIe/AON domains stayed OFF (0x600c=00) with all 9 secondaries held awake (0x077e), still reset +76 s to kernel (+85 s return). Live scan + code audit found five combined gaps: (1) 47 macOS-OFF domains (ANE_SYS/CPU, ISP_SYS, GFX, ATC3_USB, SIO_ADMA, I2C*, MTP_DMA) stayed on without force_ps; (2) old force_ps only cleared target bits 0..3 and never cleared BIT(28) AUTO_ENABLE (so ANE_SYS/CPU and GFX stayed on even when run); (3) disabling replay_mem dropped PCIe RC teardown (0x59e008000.., 0x59c000400), AMCC/SLC drain, PMP DVFS idle, AOP GPIO IRQ clear, and error-handler zeros, while qs_macos_mem.h also re-enabled APCIE_GE_SYS and SIO_CPU; (4) psci_quiesce_asc() ran after AFR/PMP/clocks went off; (5) cpu_sleep_deep_extra set IRQ_MODE=2 | FIQ_MODE=2 on CPU0 instead of keeping 0 for wake routing (unlike macOS and Ante042).

findings.title: R56A: FIRST RVBAR WAKE EVER on T6020 (image 102, 0x6004=0x22, +73 s to kernel)
findings.body: 2026-11-18 (image 102, fifth aura-ctl word 241, alarm +40 s): with all 110 macOS-OFF PMGR domains lowered including BIT(28) AUTO_ENABLE (0x6014=00, 0x601f=00, 0x600c=00, 0x6011=50), early psci_quiesce_asc(), early psci_quiesce_pcie_rc(), filtered psci_replay_mem_clean(), and WFE edge-hold (0x077e), PMU scratch 0x6004 reached 0x22 for the first time in 56 runs: CPU0 woke through RVBAR into psci_suspend_rvbar() with psci_resume.magic intact, completed psci_quiesce_undo(), armed RESUME_WDT_S, and entered Linux cpu_resume via psci_enter(). Main kernel booted at +73 s (+33 s after the +40 s alarm, earlier than every +76/+77 s WD2 reset); Linux panicked during resume as expected before resume-side fixes. Note: smp_psci_edge_release_and_sleep() calls cpu_sleep(true) directly, so CPU0 still had IRQ/FIQ_MODE=2 and still woke. Next: R56B (+90 s alarm + RVBAR PMGR SLP_S2R/elapsed/wake telemetry) to confirm genuine >60 s SLP_S2R sleep past WD2.

findings.title: R56B: FIRST REAL HARDWARE SLP_DDR SLEEP CONFIRMED (2/2 RVBAR wake); immediate wake caused by unacked SPMI_IRQ_NOTIFY (bit 54 NUB.SPMI0Sw3IRQ)
findings.body: 2026-11-18 (image 103, fifth aura-ctl word 241, alarm +90 s): RVBAR telemetry proved the SoC genuinely completed S2R entry into hardware SLP_DDR (0x6008=fe, 0x600b=fe), disarmed WD2 (0x601b=00, 0x601c=00), lost AIC state (0x601e=ff), and woke CPU0 cleanly via RVBAR (0x6004=0x22, psci_dbg[12]=1) for the second consecutive run. It woke in <1 s (0x6005/6=0000) solely on AP wake source bit 54 (0x6015=0x36, 0x6016=0x01 = NUB.SPMI0Sw3IRQ), explaining the identical +73 s return in R56A (+40 s) and R56B (+90 s) (~2 s suspend + immediate wake + ~60 s SMC wake timeout + ~11 s boot). Root cause: qs_crumb_write() never W1C-acks SPMI_IRQ_NOTIFY (0x29e114080 bit 0, verified 0x08000001 live) while spmi-apple and PSCI_S2R_SPMINOTIFY leave 0x29e114040 bit 0 enabled. Image 104 (R56C, +80 s alarm) acks 0x29e114080/0x29e154080.

findings.title: R56C: FIRST REAL HARDWARE SLP_S2R SLEEP (77 s) + RTC ALARM WAKE INTO LINUX ON M2 PRO (T6020 / J414s)!
findings.body: 2026-11-18 (image 104, fifth aura-ctl word 241, alarm +80 s): W1C-acking SPMI_IRQ_NOTIFY (0x29e114080/0x29e154080) eliminated the immediate wake from R56B. Hardware PMGR counters proved 77 FULL SECONDS in SLP_S2R (0x4d) and 77 s in SYS_S2R_AOP (0x4d), 78 s elapsed cntpct_el0 (0x004e, 18 s past WD2's 60 s bite), WD2 disarmed (ctl=00), woken cleanly by the +80 s PMU RTC alarm (sole AP wake source bit 54 NUB.SPMI0Sw3IRQ, AIC line 724), returning through RVBAR (0x6004=0x22, 3/3). Linux resumed through cpu_resume, syscore_resume, dpm_resume_noirq, and macsmc_reboot_pm_resume_early() (PMU BootErrorStage 0x6003=0x30 'OS running') before stalling ~60 s later in unported device resume (main kernel at +151 s, away 225 s). Next: Image 105 (R57A) restores psci_force_ps_lower() domains and brings all 9 cold-powered secondary CPUs back via RVBAR+CPUSTART.

findings.title: R62P: Clean non-TEST Aurora 7.3.0 + Aura 128 real S2R commit and full wake (NVMe, USB-C, SMC, Wi-Fi 54 BSSes, BT, SD, internal DCP)
findings.body: 2026-11-25 (7.3.0-s2r73+ on omacom/linux-aurora integration/aurora-7.3 + Aura image 128 with bit 20 dropped as default 0xc16dcb3f, zero aura-ctl or TEST switches): real S2R commit and RTC alarm wake (dur=34.4 s, SLP_S2R=23.10 s, 0x601f=aa, 0x6011=50 PMP+SEP gated, all 10 CPUs online). Key 7.3.0 fixes: enabled aic2_info.fw_suspend=true for AIC2 syscore save/restore, T6020 WKTP + 0x29e00400c wake mask in macsmc.c, noirq_direct SEP SLEEP with s2r_sleep_keep=afr,gpio,sep, and non-TEST internal DCP cold restart (0x7410c8+0x51c). NVMe live (31.6 MB/s), USB-C Logi Bolt live, both PCIe links up on try 1 (0x9b000211), Wi-Fi associated (ch 40, 54 BSSes), hci0 + mmc0 present, internal DCP cold-restarted (connected:1, 6 modes). Next: owner checks (BT pairing, SD card, visual display), apple_pmp/dcp_poweron + G14S aurora GPU warm restart for full desktop suspend, and overnight drain.

rules: Never remove and rescan PCI devices: it kills Wi-Fi until a reboot.
No `slpa` runs unless the owner is ready to reset the Mac by hand.
Keep a `.keep` file in module trees pacman doesn’t own.
No hotplug tests on a boot that can hurt the root filesystem.
Check the ESP sha after every copy, and refuse to suspend on the default image.
Test GRUB entries use `panic=0`, so a panic hangs and the watchdog stamps tell where it died.
unknowns: Bluetooth pairing and an SD card after the wake (the controllers come back; nothing was paired or inserted yet).
Drain in real S2R over a whole night.

upstream.what: M1 Pro (T6000) deep sleep reference by Andreas Fernandez; our comparison and question are posted on his notes commit

credits.how: His M1 Pro (T6000) suspend-to-RAM branch and notes, `t600x-s2r-reference`, are the reference we compare every step against: the SMC sequence (pmVC, WKTP, SD power around `slpa`), the NVMe/ANS cold start after the wake, the core sleep overrides and the thin stage 1.
Suspend-to-RAM groundwork on Apple silicon and the T6050/T8140 sleep work in aurora-silicon/linux: macOS traces of the sleep commit, the radio and SD reader handling, and the AP GPIO restore order.
S2R research on the M1 (m1-power-lab), the answer that iBoot arms the wake path for a raw image, and the brcmfmac D3 fixes now in linux-aurora.

Native S2R on the M2 Pro J416s and detailed answers on issue #5: the apcie re-init at the wake, the PCIe resume order, ps_sep, RVBAR locking. Also the J416s comparison of the post-wake state with macOS's (MEPS, PMU 0x200/0x1300, 0x2505, rail VR3l) and the finding that the DCP firmware must be restarted after the cut.
The T6040 AP GPIO restore order (each pin's config, then its input enable, the lock last) that Aura's wake path uses, and the warning about an interrupt storm from a reset GPIO block.
The PMP tunable headroom in m1n1 and Aura (aurora-silicon/m1n1#63, aura#268); our daily boot.bin is that build.
